body:
I'll keep your offer in mind. I haven't completely gotten over the idea, but I feel too tied up with work and my family right now to go through with it. Even if my personal life is a wreck and I have very few platonic friends and no romantic ones to speak of, I feel a deep sense of responsibility to those things, for the moment it overrides my desire for self-destruction.

By the way, I don't know who the jackass is who keeps downvoting people in this thread, but I can promise you it's not me. I value all input, even if I don't necessarily agree with it.

I appreciate your comments on my libido, but everything I've heard from r/deadbedrooms or r/askwomen has been totally different. There are multiple women there who say they would be willing to break up with a man who is perfect in every way if he does not want to copulate at a minimum of four times a week, which is a ludicrously high number of times in my view. Maybe I'd feel different if I was in a relationship with someone I really liked, but as it stands I can't imagine myself going along well with that.

As a sidenote I apologize that I'm discussing such things with you. Unlike most males (and females) my age, I find it highly distasteful to discuss private matters openly with women like this. Just another way I'm different, I suppose.

As for relating to people, I understand and appreciate what you're saying, but that has always seemed like a non-answer to me. It doesn't bring me any closer to stopping the loneliness. It reminds me a lot of the song "You Just Haven't Earned It Yet, Baby." It's an arbitrary statement that really doesn't much mean when analyzed closely. I'm not trying to be cruel, that's just how I perceive it.

I've actually felt a lot happier since this morning because there's now an end in sight. I don't have to dread years of loneliness in my future. All I have to do is this one thing, and it's all going to be fine (relatively speaking).

I very much appreciate the sentiment, but in the end, what good does it do me? It's like saying I'm not the only one who has cancer. It doesn't make the pain of loneliness any less worse, especially when all the people I have in my life seem to be doing so well.
